main:
Use case: style-transfer. Redraw the full grayscale environment tile sheet in INPUT1, art/grayscale/images/tiles_16x16.png, in beautiful pure black/white pixel art for CreatureGathererFX. INPUT2 is the crude binary version, a layout reference only.
Preserve the full 256x768 source arrangement: 16 columns and48 rows of16x16 logical tiles. Exact source positions, order, multi-tile seams, large unused black areas and every existing item must stay in the same place. Full vertical sheet aspect1:3. Prefer1024x3072 preview with logical pixels enlarged4x in hard square blocks. Do not repack or add assets. No grid overlay or labels.
Preserve original clustered round trees, stone/crystal formations, grass/reeds, flowers, mushrooms, graves, pond borders, water tiles, wooden bridges, stone wall and door, sloping roofs, wood platforms, barrels, counters, cabinets, beds, chairs, tables, fences, machinery, floor patterns, posts and small items. Multi-tile assemblies retain aligned seams. Simple repeatable terrain tiles remain simple. Empty source cells remain black.
Translate gray areas deliberately into WHITE silhouettes and BLACK carved shadows/details, chunky connected shapes, broad dark tree shadows, clear rocks, door/window cutouts, spare black roof hatching, quiet grass and water textures with isolated short dashes, distinct collectible silhouettes. Walkable terrain quieter than solid obstacles. Match polished classic monochrome handheld gathering RPG art. No threshold noise or dense checkerboard. Each feature designed to read at16x16 logical pixels. Only #000000 and#FFFFFF; NO grays, gradients, blur, antialias, color, glow, text, labels or background scenery. Output ONLY full redesigned tile sheet retaining original layout.
correction:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Input1 is the already redrawn environment tile sheet. Correct its remaining gray WATER and gray PATH patches into strict two-tone pixel art.
EVERY gray water area in the upper right must become SOLID BLACK water with only sparse WHITE short horizontal ripple dashes. EVERY gray stone/path/brick stripe in the top half must become WHITE pavement with BLACK seams defining chunky stone rectangles. Remove ALL gray from every object and background. Absolutely every pixel should be either full black #000000 or full white #FFFFFF. No gray shading anywhere, no soft edges, antialiasing or blur.
Preserve every object, all16-column48-row source tile intent, all positions and sheet dimensions/aspect1:3. Keep tree canopies, rock shapes, buildings, furniture, tiles, doors, grass and lower items unchanged except removing any incidental gray. Do not move, crop, rearrange, add labels, add objects, or fill unused blank black regions. Only correct palette and water/path texture. Output ONLY the completed full black/white sheet.
grayscaleReferenceV3: Reference: art/grayscale/images/tiles_16x16.png, indexed 2-bit palette [0,0,0], [85,85,85], [170,170,170], [255,255,255]. Redraw this exact 256x768 atlas in strict black and white with transparent empty areas; preserve the broad 16x48 16px-tile arrangement and original tile subjects. Let each source gray guide the contrast, highlight and shadow texture. Crisp square pixels, no smoothing, and no new objects. Preview only; no claim of exact tile ID or seam fidelity.

environmentClarityV4.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Redraw the supplied archived grayscale environment atlas for a 1-bit Arduboy gathering RPG, prioritizing immediate visual clarity of environment types at exactly 16x16 logical pixels per tile. Reference image is art/grayscale/images/tiles_16x16.png, 256x768 pixels, 16 columns x 48 rows. Preserve the entire source arrangement, tile subjects, exact proportions, empty black cells, multi-tile shapes, all positions, no added assets. Output 768x2304 if possible, with every logical source pixel a 3x3 hard square; the asset will be reduced to 256x768 for review. Full sheet flush to image bounds, no border/margin/grid/text. Design on a 256x768 logical canvas, NOT a high-resolution illustration. BLACK and WHITE ONLY, opaque black unused regions. Translate grayscale by redesigning silhouettes rather than noisy threshold shading. Trees: connected bold dark canopies, clean white highlights and distinct trunks. Rocks/cliffs: angular silhouettes, broad black cracks, white faces. Water/pond: black interior with only sparse horizontal white ripples, crisp shorelines. Grass: mostly white ground with sparse small black V-shaped tufts. Dirt paths: almost empty white, occasional small black pebble pairs. Stone paving: larger clean rectangular seams, no stipple noise. Roofs: strong sloped silhouettes and a few regular diagonal ribs. Walls: clear large brick outlines. Furniture: strong outlines, clean white surfaces, black gaps. Fences/bridges: thick readable rails/posts, clear walkable span. Plants/items: distinct silhouettes. Use shading only in small intentional clusters; NO dense checkerboard, NO tiny scattered dots, NO simulated gray, NO antialiasing. Avoid letting grass/water/stone/roof share one texture. Respect original 16x16 tile boundaries; preserve the bottom mostly blank area. Output only full redrawn atlas.
environmentClarityV4.export: Centered nearest-neighbor sampling to 256x768; RGB threshold 128; opaque binary output. Native dimensions do not certify authored tile positions or seams.

creatureStyleV5.prompt: Use case: style-transfer. Asset: second monochrome environment tile atlas variant for CreatureGathererFX. INPUT1 is the grayscale atlas and authoritative layout/subject reference (256x768, 16 columns x48 rows of16x16 logical tiles). INPUT2 is the current v4 environment redraw, a composition reference to refine. INPUT3 and INPUT4 are ACTUAL CREATURE SPRITES, STYLE REFERENCES ONLY. Do not add creatures or labels to the environment sheet. Redraw the full atlas to feel drawn by the same artist as those creatures: broad clean white silhouettes, bold black outlines/cutouts, friendly chunky round organic forms, elegant deliberate stepped pixel contours, minimal interior marks, large unified shadows, uncluttered surfaces. The current environment is too thin-lined, fussy and stippled. Make a clearly different second art pass with substantially cleaner, bolder forms. Trees should have rounded grouped leaf lobes, white lit crowns and chunky black undersides, sturdy simple trunks. Rocks should have large readable facets and a few black cuts. Plants should be broad leaf shapes with two or three marks rather than fine speckles. Furniture should use simple silhouettes and strong gaps. Buildings retain roof shape but use fewer wider roof ribs and larger clean brick units. Preserve environmental readability: light quiet paths; grass sparse black paired tufts; dark water with a few white horizontal ripple clusters; unmistakable banks, bridge rails, rock and wood. Retain ALL original atlas objects, exact positions, ordering, footprints, aligned multi-tile structure, full 1:3 aspect and large empty black regions. No repacking or added assets, no decorative scene, no margins. Design for 16x16 logical cells, not a high-detail illustration; prefer output 768x2304 at3x integer enlargement of256x768 logical art. Full atlas flush to edges. Strict BLACK #000000 and WHITE #FFFFFF only, opaque black unused cells. Avoid gray, antialiasing, stippling, crosshatching, dense checkerboard, gradients, glow, thin hairlines, text, creature figures. Output ONLY the redesigned environment atlas.
creatureStyleV5.export: Centered nearest-neighbor to256x768; threshold128; opaque binary. Review only; native dimensions do not certify tile IDs or seams.
